body.question: A deadly disease threatens 600 people. Treatment A: 200 people will be saved. Treatment B: a 33% chance that all 600 are saved, a 66% chance that no one is. Which did most people choose?
body.reveal: 72% chose Treatment A. But when the same outcomes were framed as deaths (A: 400 people will die; B: a 33% chance no one dies, a 66% chance all 600 die), 78% chose B. Same facts, flipped choice: the framing changed the decision.

probes.question: When the options were framed as deaths instead of lives saved, which treatment did most people pick?
True or false: in the Asian disease problem, the two framings described different outcomes.

image_brief.show: File:Glass-of-water.jpg shows a glass of water, the classic half full or half empty question

claims.claim: Deadly disease threatens 600 people; two treatments
claims.quote: Participants were asked to choose between two treatments for 600 people affected by a deadly disease.

claims.claim: Gain framing: A saves 200; B 33% chance of saving all 600, 66% chance of saving no one
claims.quote: A 33% chance of saving all 600 people, 66% possibility of saving no one.

claims.claim: 72% chose Treatment A under the lives-saved framing
claims.quote: Treatment A was chosen by 72% of participants when it was presented with positive framing ("saves 200 lives")
Treatment A was predicted to result in 400 deaths

claims.claim: Loss framing: B 33% chance no one dies, 66% chance everyone dies
claims.quote: treatment B had a 33% chance that no one would die but a 66% chance that everyone would die

claims.claim: When framed as deaths, 78% chose Treatment B (probe 1)
claims.quote: When the question was negatively framed, the result reversed, and 78% of participants chose Treatment B.

claims.claim: Same outcomes, different framings, flipped choice (probe 2: framings did not describe different outcomes)
claims.quote: Though the choices across the positive and negative framing conditions are logically equivalent, people in different conditions make different decisions.

claims.claim: It is called the Asian disease problem (probe 2)
claims.quote: the classic question, the Asian disease problem

claims.note: Verified by calculation: 600 - 200 = 400; 33% x 600 is about 200 expected saved; the page itself calls the framings logically equivalent.
